transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-11-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Aria Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Kapoor (Aurora Head of MLOps), Daniel Brooks (Aurora VP Eng), Maya Lin (Aurora SRE), Jared Kim (Aurora Platform)

Summary:
Low-level postmortem for the 11/08 production latency spike that caused elevated tail latency and 5xx errors for Aurora's real-time inference route. Discussed root cause (KV cache invalidation + autoscaler config edge case + fallback model routing), immediate mitigations applied, proposed permanent fixes, runbook and alert improvements, and next steps for a dedicated capacity pilot and load testing.

Topics:
- Incident timeline and root cause hypothesis
- Short-term and long-term mitigations
- Runbook + alerting changes
- Dedicated capacity trial and cost/latency tradeoffs
- Compliance/audit logging questions

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Goal for today is to run through the postmortem from Friday's spike, make sure we have owners and next steps — and confirm the plan for the dedicated pilot request.
[00:18] Priya: Thanks, Sofia. Big thanks for the quick patch last night, that got us back to baseline but we still saw a couple of residual timeouts for the 2nd wave.
[00:26] Liam: yeah so the tl;dr from the SE side: we observed a KV cache invalidation event triggered when a background job PR rolled out which unintentionally scrubbed some prefix keys. That forced a lot of requests to refill caches and the autoscaler config we had (scale-up cooldown 90s) couldn't keep up with the very bursty traffic. Combined with our fallback policy, some requests were routed to the larger 'redwood-genx-2' variant which drove tail latency and cost.
[00:52] Daniel: just to be clear, the fallback to the larger model — that is automatic, right? we didn't explicitly route anything.
[00:59] Liam: Correct, automatic policy. There's a compatibility mapping so when the small shard runs out or instance errors, we fallback to a compatible variant. In this case the fallback had a ~3x latency penalty.
[01:15] Maya: We also saw a few 502s from the ingress layer during the spike; looks like some connection churn during the cache refill. Some of the transcription logs show intermittent 5xx then the routing decision.
[01:30] Jared: I have to say, the autoscaler cooldown is something we set a while ago to avoid oscillation. But that 90 second window basically prevented new nodes from coming up before the cache storm subsided.
[01:43] Aria: From a CS perspective, Aurora flagged two high-value customers that noticed problems. We logged the support tickets and sent the initial customer comms — praise to the support team for the rapid acknowledgement.
[01:55] Sofia: Great. Let's walk through the timeline quick. Liam, do you want to read the timeline you sent?
[02:05] Liam: Sure. 14:07 UTC — scheduled background job deployment started; 14:09 — abnormal resp time on the training feed; 14:10 — KV invalidation event detected (pattern of prefix scrub); 14:12 — increased 5xx and latency, automatic fallback to larger variant begins; 14:15 — support escalation; 14:20 — Redwood applied emergency patch to disable the faulty invalidation job and rehydrate caches; 14:35 — partial recovery, 14:50 — baseline restored but a small % of requests still saw elevated latency until we adjusted autoscaler thresholds at 15:02. Full notes are in the incident doc we shared.
[02:40] Priya: A couple of clarifying q's: why did the invalidation job touch production prefixes? that sounds like an env var/namespace mixup.
[02:50] Liam: preliminary root cause: a deploy of a housekeeping job had a misconfigured env var (NAMESPACE override) that meant it pointed at prod prefixes for a short window during rollout. The job contained a wildcard scrub to free space and it hit some inference cache prefixes.
[03:05] Daniel: ouch. Is that a CI gating issue or a post-deploy migration step?
[03:11] Liam: It's a deployment config mistake; we should add a gating test to block wildcard scrub jobs from running against prod without a safeguard.
[03:19] Maya: on the autoscaler side, we discussed lowering the cooldown and adding burst-step scaling so we can add N nodes quickly for these prefix storms. Also maybe warm standby nodes for critical routes.
[03:33] Sofia: ok, let's split fixes into immediate and longer-term. Immediate: patch to ensure the job is disabled, adjust autoscaler to be more responsive for the inference pools, and add a manual rollback playbook. Longer-term: safer deploy gating, change fallback policy to prefer degraded responses over routing to orders-of-magnitude slower model, and add pre-warming for the critical route.
[03:58] Jared: For pre-warming, what's the overhead we're talking about? memory + cost.
[04:03] Liam: depends on the profile; for Aurora's peak we estimated ~2x baseline during busy minutes. We can propose a small warm pool that holds a few nodes per region; cost delta is manageable compared to customer impact.
[04:16] Priya: And on monitoring — we need clearer SLOs for tail latency and an alert for when fallback to larger variants exceeds X% of traffic in a 5 min window.
[04:27] Aria: We'll document that and Redwood can implement the alert in the console.
[04:30] Sofia: quick security question from Daniel — did any PII touch logs during the cache refill? we have strict handling requirements.
[04:38] Liam: we audited the logs; no PII was present in the cache keys, and the audit logs show the scrub event was internal system account. We'll share the sanitized log snippet.
[04:50] Daniel: Good. Also, we need the SOC2 evidence for the incident timeline for our compliance team.
[04:56] Aria: We'll bundle the incident timeline, audit log hashes, and the change record and put them in the secure share.
[05:02] Priya: Ok, on the runbook edits — I want a concise play for: detect cache scrub, quiesce the invalidation job, scale up inference pool, and temporarily disable fallback. Who owns the runbook change?
[05:12] Sofia: Liam + Maya to collaborate and produce a doc.
[05:17] Maya: I'll take lead on the autoscaler + staging validation.
[05:20] Liam: I'll prepare the rollback steps and the patched branch for the housekeeping job.
[05:24] Priya: timeline for that?
[05:26] Maya: I can validate thresholds and staging tests by 11/17.
[05:30] Liam: Patch will be PR'd by 11/12.
[05:34] Sofia: Great. Now the dedicated capacity pilot — Priya you asked for a 2-week window to measure tail behavior, right?
[05:42] Priya: Yes, it's to see if isolated capacity removes the variable of noisy neighbors and autoscaler lag. Also we'd like to test the pre-warm strategy.
[05:50] Sofia: Redwood will send pricing and SLOs for the pilot. We usually do a small credit and then a short reserved window; we'll include metrics to track.
[05:58] Daniel: one ask — we want a benchmark harness we can run with our traffic patterns.
[06:03] Liam: We'll export a small harness and a dataset scaffold; it's not a full replay but should mimic your percentiles. We'll coordinate with Jared for the exact request distribution.
[06:12] Jared: I'll provide request traces and the top 10 user journeys by 11/13.
[06:18] Aria: On comms — we'll coordinate a joint message to affected customers once we have the timeline and the mitigation plan. Keep it concise and focused on actions taken.
[06:28] Priya: Good. A couple more ops notes: 1) add a safety flag in CI to prevent wildcard prod scrubs, 2) make the fallback policy explicit per-route in the console UI, 3) add an audit for cache invalidation events with an auto-ticket when scrub exceeds threshold.
[06:50] Liam: For the console UI item, it's on our roadmap but we can prioritize a per-route toggle as an interim.
[06:58] Daniel: Any blockers to the pilot? procurement or legal?
[07:02] Aria: Redwood has a standard pilot agreement; legal said no extra risk. We will however need an NDA addendum for the audit logs bundle; we'll push that through.
[07:12] Priya: ok, let's do a quick risk rating — how likely is recurrence if we do nothing?
[07:18] Liam: medium-high because the root cause is a human-deploy config issue; without CI guardrails it could happen again. With the immediate mitigations recurrence risk drops to low.
[07:29] Maya: we should also run a failure injection test — simulate cache invalidation in staging and verify autoscaler + fallback behavior.
[07:36] Sofia: We'll add that to action items.
[07:39] (small cross talk)
[07:45] Daniel: about cost — if we go to dedicated capacity, what's the delta in ops cost and unit token cost?
[07:52] Sofia: we'll provide a comparative spreadsheet; in past pilots customers saw lower tail latency and more predictable costs, though nominal unit cost can be higher if you reserve. We'll include an estimate.
[08:05] Priya: For the compliance package Aria mentioned, can we get the audit log retention options? we may want 1 year.
[08:12] Aria: Yes, Redwood has add-on options for extended retention; we'll surface pricing in the same doc.
[08:19] Liam: Quick note on telemetry — we'd like to add a graph for fallback-percentage over time and a per-route cache-hit ratio. These will help in post-incident triage.
[08:30] Priya: Agreed.
[08:34] Sofia: Alright let's do a recap of next steps — I'll read them out. Redwood: send incident timeline + sanitized logs (Sofia/Aria), send pilot pricing and SLOs (Sofia), share patched branch and rollback steps (Liam), share benchmark harness and coordinate traces (Liam + Jared). Aurora: confirm priority flows (Priya), validate alerts + runbook in staging (Maya). We'll reconvene 11/18 for a quick check-in.
[09:05] Daniel: sounds good. One more small item — can we get an explicit note about no PII exposure for compliance?
[09:12] Aria: yes we'll include a signed statement and the audit hashes.
[09:16] Priya: ok thanks everyone.
[09:20] Sofia: thanks team. We'll follow up with the docs and next steps.
[09:25] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription quality: there are a few mis-heard words around specific internal job names and model variant ids — we've left them generalized in the recording to avoid confusion.
